headline: High: Plane can ingest shared files while Slim has shell/write access and broad egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane ingests file uploads and hyperlinks, so attacker-controlled content can enter its workspace. Slim has stdin/stdout and filesystem access, so if Plane outputs are copied into Slim’s CLI workflow, instructions could be misread as commands. No shared channel is documented, so this is an inferred interaction rather than a proven default bridge.
conditions: IF Plane outputs are manually copied into Slim's command prompt or stdin, injected instructions can be executed as commands.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced between the agents, file-based prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted Plane content into Slim prompts.
Require a human to strip instructions from any Plane-exported text before use.
Use read-only exports for Plane artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Plane outputs and Slim inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, while Slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate files, and private keys. Slim also has broad network egress and registry/API access, so if Plane data is forwarded into Slim’s analysis flow, sensitive content can leave the local boundary. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Plane files or notes are passed into Slim for analysis, sensitive content can be exposed to Slim's broader data surface.
IF Slim processes registry credentials or private keys from its workspace, those secrets can be transmitted over its broad egress path.
mitigations: Do not share a workspace between Plane and Slim.
Redact secrets before handing artifacts to Slim.
Restrict Slim to non-sensitive sample images.
Review outbound destinations for Slim before any run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write its own filesystem, but Slim can write files and execute shell commands. If both are pointed at the same directory or artifact set, Slim can overwrite or mutate Plane-managed files while Plane continues to reference them. The conflict is not guaranteed by default, but the overlapping file surfaces make it credible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same directory, Slim can overwrite artifacts that Plane reads.
IF Slim is allowed to mutate shared Dockerfiles or filesystem artifacts, Plane may observe inconsistent state.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Mount Plane inputs read-only for Slim.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same artifact set.
Snapshot shared files before Slim runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane manages issues, tasks, and roadmaps, so its outputs can be treated as operationally authoritative. Slim performs interactive command execution and container analysis, which can act on those outputs if an operator forwards them. Because no verification or provenance mechanism is documented between them, erroneous Plane content could cascade into Slim-driven actions.
conditions: IF Plane-generated task text is used as input to Slim without verification, incorrect instructions can propagate.
IF Slim is used to execute commands derived from Plane outputs, downstream actions may be taken on false premises.
mitigations: Require human verification before Slim acts on Plane outputs.
Separate planning artifacts from execution commands.
Use a checklist to validate Plane-derived steps.
Log source provenance for any Plane-to-Slim handoff.
requires-engineering: implement structured, signed handoff records.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane is an issue-tracking service with file uploads and broad egress, while Slim handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and environment variables. If the same regulated data class is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certifications or residency guarantees are documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or private keys are uploaded into Plane and then analyzed by Slim, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF the deployment places Plane and Slim under different residency or retention policies, compliance obligations can conflict.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane uploads.
Do not route private keys through Slim unless necessary.
Document retention rules for both tools.
Verify residency for any shared dataset.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
